sections.h2: Which offices deal with property tax in Wayne County, KY?
sections.html:
Wayne County splits the job three ways, all in Monticello. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) decides what each parcel is worth, the Sheriff collects the bill during the regular season, and the County Clerk inherits whatever remains unpaid after April 15.

The PVA works from 55 N. Main Street, Suite 107, Monticello, KY 42633, and answers at 606-348-6621. The county lists weekday hours of 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. and also opens on the first and third Saturday of each month from 8 a.m. to noon, which helps owners who work during the week and want to ask about an assessment or file for an exemption. For payment questions or a bill that did not arrive, ask the Sheriff's Office in Monticello for its current number and window hours.

The PVA does not set the rate you pay. The fiscal court, the school board, and special taxing districts vote those, and the PVA's job ends with the assessed value.

sections.h2: What are the payment deadlines for a Wayne County tax bill?
sections.html:
Bills are payable to the Sheriff until April 15, and the cost climbs in steps set by KRS 134.015. A homeowner who pays in full by November 1 takes 2 percent off. After January 31 the penalty reaches 10 percent. The County Clerk's office takes over unpaid bills the next day.

  • By November 1: discount of 2 percent on the amount due.
  • November 2 through December 31: the bill as printed.
  • January: 5 percent penalty on the unpaid tax.
  • February through April 15: 10 percent penalty on the unpaid tax.

If the state mails bills late, the Department of Revenue can replace that calendar with one that gives 30 days for each step. Ask the Sheriff which calendar applies to the current bill before you count days.

sections.h2: How does a Wayne County owner appeal an assessment?
sections.html:
Start with a conference at the PVA, because Kentucky does not let you file an appeal without one. The PVA must walk you through how the number was built and write up the meeting. Wayne County owners then follow the statewide calendar.

Wayne County assessment appeal sequence (Kentucky Department of Revenue)
StepTiming
Tax roll open for inspection13 days from the first Monday in May
Conference with the PVABefore filing; can start when notices are mailed
File appeal at the County ClerkBy close of business the day after inspection ends
Local board of assessment appeals25 to 35 days after inspection ends, up to five days

Bring proof to the board: a description of the land and buildings, insurance policies, what it cost to build, and recent sales listings. Without that, the board must deny the appeal. A written explanation follows any increase or decrease. Skipping the hearing after filing ends your right to go further to the Kentucky Claims Commission. For lake-area parcels, comparable sales and the physical condition of docks, decks and outbuildings on January 1 are the facts that carry weight.

sections.h2: Is there a tax break for older or disabled Wayne County owners?
sections.html:
Yes. Homeowners aged 65 or older, and those classified as totally disabled by a federal or retirement program, can apply for the homestead exemption. For 2025 and 2026 it removes $49,100 from the assessed value of the home they live in.

Wayne County's Census median owner-occupied value is $135,700, so a typical qualifying house would be taxed on $86,600. At the state's 2025 real property rate of 10.6 cents per $100, the state portion falls from roughly $143.84 to roughly $91.80. Local rates come on top and vary by district, so the PVA is the place to get the combined figure for a specific address.

  • Apply at the Wayne County PVA, in the year you want the relief.
  • Age is shown with a birth certificate, driver's license, passport, or other approved document.
  • Disability must come from a federal agency or retirement system, with payments received for the whole assessment period.
  • Veterans with a service-connected disability and people found totally and permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems do not need to reapply every year.

sections.h2: What if Wayne County property tax is unpaid when I sell?
sections.html:
A sale does not wipe the debt. The tax is personal to the owner from the assessment date, and the lien on the parcel lasts up to 11 years no matter who holds the deed. Expect the title company to find it and ask for payment from your proceeds.

Once April 15 passes, the Sheriff hands the bill to the County Clerk as a certificate of delinquency. The face amount gets a 10 percent penalty and the sheriff's add-on, then interest at 1 percent a month, a clerk commission, and a lien recording fee. A county attorney commission and mailing costs join the total after the notice stage. Revenue's worked example turns a $1,000 bill into $1,254 at the handoff and about $1,611 after the first notice.

A tax sale can follow 90 to 135 days after the transfer. A third-party buyer who takes the certificate can add fees, which is why paying the Sheriff before April 15 is the cheaper route. Splitting the current-year bill is a negotiation item in the contract, so write down who pays what.

sections.h2: What does a seller in Wayne County, Kentucky need to know about the area?
sections.html:
Wayne County sits on the Tennessee line, formed on December 13, 1800 from Pulaski and Cumberland counties and named for General Anthony Wayne. Monticello is the only city and the seat. About 458 square miles of land fall within the county, which reaches into the Daniel Boone National Forest and borders Lake Cumberland, which the county's own site credits with 1,255 miles of shoreline. Mill Springs, where the Battle of Mill Springs took place on January 19, 1862, is in the county as well.

Time is a practical issue: Wayne County is on Eastern time, but its western and southern edges follow the Eastern and Central boundary, so out-of-county buyers or lenders may be an hour apart. Wayne County Schools runs the public system; Monticello Independent merged into it on June 30, 2013.

  • 2025 population: 19,597, up 0.2 percent from 2020 and below the 20,813 counted in 2010.
  • 10,206 housing units for 8,074 households.
  • 69.1 percent owner-occupied; median home value $135,700.
  • Median household income $45,739; 28.8 percent of residents in poverty.
  • Median gross rent $727.

The 2,132 units beyond the household count mean plenty of homes are not someone's full-time residence. Owners with an inherited lake cabin, a rental, or a house needing work can sell as-is for cash and have tax and lien payoffs handled at closing.

faqs.q: Where is the Wayne County PVA office?
faqs.a: It is at 55 N. Main Street, Suite 107, in Monticello, and the phone is 606-348-6621. The office is open weekdays from 8 to 4 and on the first and third Saturday from 8 to noon.

faqs.q: What is the discount for paying Wayne County property tax early?
faqs.a: Two percent, for paying the full bill by November 1. The face amount applies through December 31, then 5 percent in January and 10 percent after that.

faqs.q: Do I have to meet with the PVA before appealing in Wayne County?
faqs.a: Yes. Kentucky requires a conference with the PVA or a deputy before an appeal can be filed with the County Clerk, and the filing is due by close of business the day after the inspection period ends.

faqs.q: How much is the homestead exemption in Wayne County?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years, taken off the assessed value of your home. You must be 65 or older, or totally disabled, and apply at the PVA.

faqs.q: What happens to Wayne County taxes still owed after April 15?
faqs.a: They move to the County Clerk as a certificate of delinquency with a lien. Penalties, 1 percent monthly interest, and commissions are added, and the certificate can be sold to a third party 90 to 135 days later.
